highlights.text: Does this place have decent food?” “Does it matter?” Hadrian chuckled. “I’d be happy for a bit of three-day-ripe field mouse at this point.
“See,” Royce said, irritated, “this is the problem with these good deeds of yours; they never end.”
“You’re not going to charge us for the tower, I hope,” Hadrian said. “But if you are, it was Royce’s fault and should come out of his share.”
No, it’s best to avoid killing nobles.” “At least not where there are witnesses,” Royce said with a grin.
“And you could be the infamous marquis Melborn.” “Why infamous?” “Would you prefer notorious? Nefarious, perhaps?” “What’s wrong with beloved?”
You don’t win battles with hate. Anger and hate can make you brave, make you strong, but they also make you stupid. You end up tripping over your own two feet.”

“I had hoped to be gone before it returned,” Royce said. “Not possible. Besides, this shouldn’t be a problem for you, of all people. I am certain you have stolen from occupied homes before.” “Not ones where the owner can swallow me in a single bite.” “So we’ll have to be extra quiet now, won’t we?”
